title: Information-sharing practices on Facebook during the 2017 French presidential campaign: An "unreliable information bubble" within the extreme right
screen_reason: Observational analysis of 1,146,784 posts from 252 French political Facebook pages and groups (Oct 2016-May 2017). Of the 133,261 link-sharing posts whose source could be rated for reliability against the Decodex source list, 86.06% (114,679) came from reliable sources and 18,582 from unreliable sources - a share of SHARED links carrying unreliable sources, with an explicit denominator. Per the governing denominator rule, '% of shared links unreliable' is SHARING (content_share).

estimates.platform: Facebook (252 pages and public groups of five political communities: LFI, PS, REM, LR, FN)
estimates.measure_type: % of reliability-coded link shares on French political Facebook pages/groups that came from sources classified unreliable
estimates.value_raw: 18,582 unreliable of 133,261 reliability-coded publications (Table 2: Reliable N = 114 679, Unreliable N = 18 582; text: 'our analysis is based on a significant number of publications (133,261)'; the complementary reliable share is printed as 86.06%)
estimates.denominator: 133,261 link-sharing Facebook publications from the 252 sampled political pages/groups whose linked source could be rated reliable or unreliable (37.49% of the 355,503 source occurrences; the full corpus is 1,146,784 posts, of which 31% contained an external link)
estimates.definition: The post linked to a domain classified 'unreliable' in the Decodex database, i.e. a French news website, blog or activist site shown by fact-checkers and journalists to have published disinformation or misinformation in the past (the authors merged Decodex's 'reliable' and 'rather reliable' into one reliable category, leaving 'unreliable' as the numerator)
estimates.misinfo_def: "we analyze the propagation of potential sources of disinformation and misinformation, labelling them together as unreliable information by referencing the different types of sources (i. e., unreliable sources) that have published or shared this kind of content in the past (news websites, blogs, activists' websites, etc.)"
estimates.source_quote: It appears that 86.06 % (114,679) of the content shared within our sample set has been shared from reliable sources (Table 2).
estimates.page_loc: Results, section 'The reliability and the ideological diversity of information sources...', p. 659; Table 2, p. 660; Methods p. 657
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Decodex, the Le Monde journalists' database of French information sources, which classifies domains as reliable / rather reliable / unreliable (unreliable = having relayed false information or disinformation in the past); the authors merged reliable + rather reliable. Only sources with more than 10 occurrences were coded (95.04% of source occurrences), and reliability could be assigned to only 37.49% of them. A Cohen's kappa of 0.959 is reported for three researchers coding a random sample, but the text says that test measured agreement on the POLITICAL AFFILIATION of a URL, not on reliability.
estimates.moderator_quote: "Our objective here is not to identify actual disinformation and misinformation propagation, as we do not examine the precise content shared in the Facebook groups of our sample, but the potential risk of dissemination of unreliable information derived by the use of specific sources. In order to identify these unreliable sources, we use a database1 that references unreliable French news websites which have been shown to publish disinformation or misinformation according to French fact-checkers and journalists."
estimates.notes: The unreliable share is not printed; it is an exact part/whole share from two verbatim counts with the same denominator (18,582/133,261 = 13.94%), which R8 allows. It is NOT the complement 100 - 86.06 computed from a percentage: Table 2 gives the unreliable count directly and 114,679 + 18,582 = 133,261 confirms the denominator. IMPORTANT CAVEAT for pooling: the denominator is only the 37.49% of shared sources that Decodex could rate; political-institution and activist websites are largely unrated, and the authors say those are exactly where FN's unreliable content concentrates, so the true unreliable share of ALL link shares is not identified by this figure (it could go either way). population_scope coded 'other' because the sharers are party community managers and partisan activists running official/local party pages and public partisan groups, not a general-public sample.

missed_or_uncertain: 1) Per-community reliability shares exist only as Figure 2 (a bar chart); the text and Table 2 give standardized residuals (LFI 63.22, PS 22.50, REM -16.91, LR 5.52, FN -117.66) and a Cramer's V of 0.342, not percentages, so no country x community rows can be extracted. The FN result - the paper's headline 'unreliable information bubble' - is therefore not available as a number in this text. 2) Ideological-alignment percentages (LFI 88.71%, FN 74.96%, LR 34.49% non-aligned, PS 18.91%) and endo-citation rates (FN 96%, LFI 93%, LR 84%, PS 74%, REM 25% far-right / 13% far-left) are shares of politically ALIGNED sources, not of unreliable ones, so they are not misinformation estimates. 3) Source-type shares (social media 42% / 124,569 posts, press 24% / 71,577, political institutions within LFI 19%, FN activist sites 11% and blogs 12%) classify source TYPE, not veracity. 4) '31% of these posts contained a link' is a corpus-composition figure. 5) No CONCENTRATION estimate: the paper never reports a top-X% of pages or sources accounting for Y% of unreliable sharing, so R1 cannot be met.

rob.design: Observational Facebook trace study. 75 interviews with party supporters and community managers were used to identify the 252 most active Facebook pages and public groups of five political communities (LFI, PS, REM, LR, FN; roughly 50 per community, at national, regional and departmental level). Netvizz extracted 1,146,784 posts published Oct 2016-May 2017; 31% contained an external link and only those are analysed. Sources with more than 10 occurrences (95.04%, 355,503) were manually categorised; source TYPE could be coded for 82.20% (292,210), RELIABILITY for only 37.49% (133,261) and political affiliation for 15.00% (53,327). Reliability came from the Decodex list (reliable / rather reliable / unreliable), with the first two merged. Cohen's kappa = 0.959 across three researchers on a random sample, reported for political-affiliation coding. No sampling of users or of the wider platform; no response rate concept. Non-link posts (statuses, native video, photos, events) are outside the frame, and the authors state they did not inspect the content shared, only the reliability of its source.
rob.item6_quote: This entailed identifying and distinguishing reliable sources – those engaged in fact-checking or the journalistic task of verification – from unreliable or hardly reliable sources (those having relayed false information or disinformation in the past).
rob.item10_quote: It appears that 86.06 % (114,679) of the content shared within our sample set has been shared from reliable sources (Table 2).
